props.title: Vampire's Kiss
props.initialSlug: Unhinged exec believes he's becoming a vampire

sections.content: Vampire's Kiss (1989) represents Nicolas Cage at his most unhinged, delivering a gloriously deranged performance as Peter Loew, a literary agent descending into vampire-themed madness. The film brilliantly blurs the line between psychological thriller and dark comedy, predating the meta-horror approach of Scream (1996) by deliberately playing with vampire movie tropes. Cage's infamous cockroach-eating scene and his increasingly manic behavior - including his unforgettable "A-B-C" recitation - established this as a cult classic that influenced later psychological horror-comedies like American Psycho (2000).

sections.content: The film's brilliant exploration of toxic masculinity and corporate culture predates similar themes in Fight Club (1999) and American Psycho (2000). Peter Loew's descent mirrors Patrick Bateman's, both characters trapped in the soul-crushing world of 1980s Manhattan executives. Director Robert Bierman uses vampire mythology as a metaphor for workplace predation and sexual power dynamics, themes later explored in films like The Wolf of Wall Street (2013).

Cage's performance style in Vampire's Kiss became a blueprint for his later "Cage Rage" roles, influencing his work in Face/Off (1997) and Bad Lieutenant: Port of Call New Orleans (2009). His commitment to physical comedy and psychological breakdown scenes created a unique acting approach that would define much of his career and influence a generation of performers willing to push boundaries between comedy and horror. sections.content: Vampire's Kiss created a template for unconventional vampire stories that questioned reality versus delusion, influencing films like Shadow of the Vampire (2000) and Only Lovers Left Alive (2013). The film's approach to vampire mythology as metaphor for mental illness and addiction opened doors for more experimental takes on the genre, including A Girl Walks Home Alone at Night (2014) and Let the Right One In (2008).
